name: RULER
description: Realistic and Universal Long-context Evaluation for Models goes beyond simple needle-in-a-haystack retrieval to evaluate long-context reasoning across four task categories: retrieval (single/multi-key), multi-hop tracing (variable tracking across documents), aggregation (frequent item identification), and question answering. Measures the 'effective context length' — the length beyond which reasoning performance degrades below a threshold.
evaluation_method: accuracy at various context lengths (4K–128K+ tokens)
typical_sota_score: ~90–96% at 128K tokens (best proprietary models); open-source models often collapse at 64K+
reputation: Key benchmark for validating claimed context window lengths; developed by NVIDIA; reveals that many models claiming 32K+ contexts fail to maintain performance at those lengths; widely cited in long-context model evaluations
notes: Introduced the concept of 'effective context length' — distinguishing claimed from actual usable context. Configurable across lengths from 4K to 128K+ tokens. Revealed significant gap between proprietary and open-source models. Models like Jamba 1.5 and Gemini 1.5 Pro maintain >94% at 128K; Mistral Large 2 drops to 48.1% at 128K. Published 2024 by NVIDIA.
